definitions.definition: One Brahman alone exists, but as qualified: souls and matter are its real, inseparable modes and body; hence difference and non-difference are both true, the former of the modes, the latter of the one qualified whole.

relations.note: the positive doctrine against which Advaita's avidyā is rejected

name: The body–self relation of world and God (śarīra–śarīrin)

definitions.definition: All souls and matter are the Lord's body — wholly controlled, supported and existing for him — and he is their self; this relation, taught by the mediating texts, explains how Brahman is one and yet the world and souls are real and distinct.

members: the Lord as self (śarīrin, ādhāra, niyantṛ, śeṣin)
souls and matter as body (śarīra, ādheya, niyāmya, śeṣa)

definitions.definition: The relation between substance and mode, Brahman and its body, substance and attribute: the second can neither exist nor be known without the first, though distinct from it; it replaces both identity and the Nyāya inherence (samavāya).

Words with different grounds of application referring to one object; the key to reading identity-texts ('tat tvam asi', 'sarvaṃ khalv idaṃ brahma') as naming one Brahman under different modes, since a word denoting a mode ultimately denotes the substance it qualifies.

name: The three realities (tattvatraya: cit, acit, Īśvara)

definitions.definition: Three eternal, real and distinct entities: souls, insentient matter and the Lord, the first two being the body of the third.

name: Brahman's twofold mark (ubhaya-liṅga): free of all defect, full of auspicious qualities

definitions.definition: Brahman is at once opposed to all that is evil and the sole abode of infinite auspicious qualities; 'nirguṇa' texts deny only prākṛta, defiling qualities, so Brahman is both 'nirguṇa' and 'saguṇa' in these two senses.

relations.note: the Lord is free of prakṛti's guṇas

definitions.definition: Countless unsurpassed qualities: the six (knowledge, power, lordship, strength, virility, splendour) and those that make him approachable — compassion, motherly love, gracious condescension, accessibility, lordship; they belong to him in every form.

relations.note: the Pāñcarātra's six are the core set

name: The five forms of God (para, vyūha, vibhava, antaryāmin, arcā)

definitions.definition: The one Lord is present as the supreme (para) in Vaikuṇṭha, the four vyūhas, the descents (vibhava), the inner controller (antaryāmin) and the consecrated image (arcā), in ascending order of accessibility; the arcā is the most accessible.

Vāsudeva (all six qualities), Saṅkarṣaṇa (knowledge and strength), Pradyumna (lordship and virility), Aniruddha (power and splendour), with functions in creation, maintenance, dissolution and teaching, and as objects of meditation.

name: The two realms of the Lord (nitya-vibhūti and līlā-vibhūti)

definitions.definition: The Lord's domain is twofold: the eternal realm of pure sattva (Vaikuṇṭha), a quarter beyond, and the realm of play made of prakṛti and time, where the world is created and souls transmigrate.

name: The three kinds of insentient reality

definitions.definition: Pure sattva (śuddha-sattva), mixed sattva (prakṛti with the three guṇas and its twenty-three evolutes — mahat, ahaṃkāra, mind, ten senses, five subtle and five gross elements) and that devoid of sattva (time).
Six substances — prakṛti, time, pure sattva, attributive consciousness, soul, Lord — and ten non-substances — sattva, rajas, tamas, sound, touch, form, taste, smell, conjunction and potency.

Consciousness as an attribute of the self, distinct from the self-luminous self that has it: eternal, it contracts through karma in bondage and expands to omniscience in release; it reveals objects to its owner and is manifest only to him.
The referent of 'I' is the soul itself, not the ego-evolute of prakṛti; the 'I' persists in deep sleep and in release.

relations.note: the self known as 'I'; rejects the Advaita view that the 'I' is a superimposition

definitions.definition: Eternal, atomic, self-luminous as 'I', a knower with attributive consciousness, an agent dependent on the Lord, an enjoyer, essentially his servant (śeṣa), a mode of Brahman; countless, and remaining distinct in liberation.
Bound (baddha), freed (mukta) and eternal (nitya); bound souls seek enjoyment or release, and seekers of release seek kaivalya or the Lord, by bhakti or prapatti.
Five kinds: eternal, freed, bound, isolated (kevala, those in kaivalya) and seekers of release (mumukṣu).

name: Master and servant (śeṣī–śeṣa): the soul's belonging to the Lord

definitions.definition: The soul's essential nature is to exist for the Lord, its master (śeṣin); all its good lies in his pleasure and its fulfilment in service.
Emphasis on belonging to the Lord alone (ananyārha-śeṣatva) and on total dependence (pāratantrya), such that even one's surrender is not one's own act of means.

name: Mind and its parts in Viśiṣṭādvaita

definitions.definition: Mind (manas), intellect (mahat/buddhi) and ahaṃkāra are evolutes of prakṛti and instruments of the soul; the actual knowing is the soul's attributive consciousness working through them; ahaṃkāra as evolute is distinct from the true 'I', the self.
Sattva, rajas and tamas are qualities (non-substances) of prakṛti, mixed in all bodies and worlds; the Lord and the eternal realm are free of them.
Eternal, real, insentient matter with three guṇas (mixed sattva), the Lord's body; called māyā for its wonderful effects, not because it is illusory.
An eternal insentient substance without guṇas, part of the Lord's body, ruling change in the realm of play and present but not ruling in the eternal realm.

name: Brahman as material and efficient cause through its body

definitions.definition: In dissolution Brahman has souls and matter as a subtle body without name and form; in creation, as a gross body with name and form; Brahman is thus the material and efficient cause, and the transformation is real, yet belongs to the body, leaving Brahman untouched.

relations.note: the effect is a real state of the existent cause

definitions.definition: The effect is the cause in another state: the world is Brahman-with-body in gross state, pre-existing as Brahman-with-body in subtle state; transformation is real (pariṇāma), not apparent (vivarta).

name: Creation and dissolution as the Lord's play

definitions.definition: Creation, maintenance and dissolution are the Lord's play (līlā) in the realm of prakṛti: he creates to give souls bodies to work out karma and seek him; Brahmā and Śiva are souls whom he empowers; the eternal realm is untouched by these cycles.

The Lord's descents are real, taken by his will in bodies of pure sattva, not from karma, for protecting the good, destroying evil and above all for being accessible; knowing their divinity liberates. Principal (mukhya) descents are the Lord himself; secondary (gauṇa) are empowered souls.

name: Apprehension of the real (satkhyāti) — the Viśiṣṭādvaita theory of error

definitions.definition: Every cognition is of something real; error is incomplete apprehension, not the appearance of the unreal or indescribable; explained by the triplication of elements and, in dreams, by the Lord's creation.
Three: perception, inference, scripture; all have qualified objects; the Lord is known from scripture alone.

name: Texts of difference, non-difference and mediation

definitions.definition: Scripture speaks of difference (bheda), of non-difference (abheda) and of the body–self relation (ghaṭaka); the last reconciles the first two, so that no text need be set aside as figurative or lower.

name: Scripture and its authority in Viśiṣṭādvaita

definitions.definition: The Veda is authorless and eternal, re-promulgated by the Lord in each creation; it alone makes the Lord known; the Itihāsa–Purāṇas (above all the Viṣṇu Purāṇa) and the Pāñcarātra, spoken by the Lord, are authoritative, and the Tamil hymns of the Āḻvārs are a Veda in Tamil.

name: The unity of Pūrva and Uttara Mīmāṃsā (aikaśāstrya)

definitions.definition: Ritual inquiry and inquiry into Brahman are one science; the first prepares for the second, and rightly read presupposes the Lord.
In deep sleep the self rests in the Lord within the heart, its knowledge contracted; it persists as 'I', as the memory 'I slept happily' shows.
Dream objects are created by the Lord for the dreamer's experience of the fruits of karma; they are real for their duration and for the dreamer alone.

name: Departure of the soul at death

definitions.definition: The knower or surrendered soul leaves through the channel of the head, the Lord in the heart illuminating the way; others leave by other channels to further births.
The bhakti-yogin must remember the Lord at death; for the surrendered the Lord himself remembers and leads them, so no last remembrance is needed (the fourth of Varadarāja's six sayings).

name: The path of light (arcirādi-gati)

definitions.definition: All who reach Brahman travel after death by the path of light — flame, day, bright fortnight, northern course, year, wind, sun, moon, lightning, then Varuṇa, Indra and Prajāpati as escorts — cross the Virajā and enter Vaikuṇṭha.

notes: Order and list of stations recalled; check against Śrībhāṣya 4.3 and the Arcirādi.

definitions.definition: The temples sung by the Āḻvārs, where the Lord abides as the image; visiting and praying for his welfare (maṅgaḷāśāsana) at them is a Śrīvaiṣṇava practice.
